A signal to turn left or make a U-turn is given by the left arm stretched out horizontally to the side, or the right arm stretched out to the side and bent upwards at a right angle at the elbow. A signal to turn right is given by the right arm stretched out horizontally to the side, or the left arm stretched out to the side and bent upwards at a right angle at the elbow. A braking signal is given by raising the left or right arm vertically upwards. A signal with the direction indicator or by hand must be given in good time, before starting the manoeuvre, and must stop immediately after the manoeuvre is completed (a hand signal may stop immediately before the manoeuvre begins). The signal must not mislead other road users. Giving a signal with the direction indicator or by hand does not give the driver priority and does not release them from the duty to take the necessary precautions.
